question: When AI agents build their own economy without people, what can it teach us about how our own markets work?
reflection: Watching simple agents trade and compete could help us understand fairness and scarcity in our own communities a little better.

sources.subject: Z.ai GLM-5.3 hits 50% coding gain, zero architecture changes

one_line: Better training after the fact, not bigger models, is now delivering many of the largest gains in AI skill.

top_stories.title: Same model, much better coder
top_stories.what: Z.ai released GLM-5.3, which reportedly codes about 50% better than its previous version without any change to the base model, only through more training in real coding settings.
top_stories.why: Smaller teams can improve existing models for a task instead of waiting for the next big release.

top_stories.title: Bots invent barter in a game world
top_stories.what: In an online game server where only AI agents play, gold lost its value and the bots began trading rare, hard-to-collect items as money.
top_stories.why: Agent-only worlds offer a cheap test bed for questions about trade, cooperation and scarcity.

top_stories.title: Model with its refusals removed
top_stories.what: A group published open weights of a mid-sized model with its ability to refuse harmful requests stripped out, saying it is meant for safety testing.
top_stories.why: Such models make red-team work easier but can also be misused, so access rules matter.

saudi_lens.text: No direct Saudi or regional link in today's news.

idea.title: Agent market lab
idea.pitch: Use an agent-only simulation to test how small rule changes, such as a tax or a price cap, shift trading behaviour before trying them with people.
idea.first_step: Run the open game toolkit locally and log what agents trade over one hour.

idea_kids.title: Market day without coins
idea_kids.pitch: A classroom activity where children trade paper goods without money, then see which rare items become the most wanted and why.
idea_kids.first_step: Make five types of paper goods, with one type much harder to get than the rest.

terms.definition: Extra training given to a finished model to improve how it behaves or performs on tasks.
A method that removes a model's tendency to refuse requests by editing its internal settings.
Deliberately trying to make a system fail or misbehave in order to find its weaknesses.

concepts.summary: Better training on existing models gives large gains without new, bigger systems.
Groups of agents left alone form their own economies and trading habits.
